note: Recipes describe how to add an external corpus to CLARION. 'context_origin' says what translator context the source can actually supply: 'native' means the upstream project wrote real translator comments, msgctxt, intents or references and the importer only maps them onto CLIFF fields; 'derived' means the corpus is flat sentence pairs and context is computed deterministically from document ids, domain labels and neighbouring segments; 'none' means it carries no context and may only be used in the plain arm or as a metric calibration set. A model annotation pass ('clarion corpus fetch --annotate') can add a brief to a derived source, and every item it touches is marked context_origin=annotated until a human signs it off. Track A (tier 'vendor') may be committed to this repository after fetching, with attribution and the licence file the recipe names. Track B (tier 'fetch-only' and 'sharealike') is written outside the repository or into a segregated directory and is never committed. Nothing here is downloaded automatically: run 'python -m clarion corpus fetch <id>'.

recipes.title: WMT24++ human post-edited references
recipes.notes: Professional post-edited references with document ids and domain labels (news, social, speech, literary). The only established MT benchmark that is safely redistributable in an MIT repository. Released 2025, so contamination is lower than FLORES.

recipes.title: San kuo (Romance of the Three Kingdoms), Chinese original with Brewitt-Taylor's 1925 translation
recipes.notes: Classical Chinese chapter-novel prose with a professional 1925 English translation. Both sides are public domain and both are archaic in their own language, which is what the classical-to-classical requirement means for localization. Only the opening chapters are imported. Paragraph alignment is proposed by a model as index pairs and then verified: indices must exist, the mapping must be strictly increasing on both sides, and the length ratio must be plausible. Brewitt-Taylor translates freely, so unverifiable pairs are dropped rather than repaired.

recipes.title: Hung Lou Meng (Dream of the Red Chamber), Chinese original with Joly's 1892 translation
recipes.notes: The opening chapter of the greatest Qing-dynasty novel with H. Bencraft Joly's 1892 translation. Long continuous narrative with a strong emotional register; both sides public domain. Same verified index alignment as the Three Kingdoms recipe.

recipes.title: FLORES+ multi-parallel evaluation set
recipes.notes: Multi-parallel, so the same sources exist in every language. ShareAlike: our segmentation is an adaptation, so the derived files must be published under CC-BY-SA-4.0 in a segregated directory. Known to be contaminated; use it for comparability, not for absolute claims.

recipes.title: Godot editor localization (gettext PO with translator comments)
recipes.notes: Real product UI strings with #. translator comments and msgctxt disambiguation, under a permissive licence. Imported through pycliff.from_po, so the CLIFF context fields come from the PO comments.

recipes.title: Mozilla Firefox localization (Fluent with comment levels)
recipes.notes: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft and may live in an MIT repository as long as the files keep their licence header, so keep them in datasets/mpl-2.0/.

recipes.title: Unciv game translations
recipes.notes: Units, technologies, tutorials and quotes with in-file context comments. The most permissively licensed game corpus with real Chinese translations.

recipes.title: Creative Commons 4.0 legal code, official translations
recipes.license: public domain (Creative Commons dedicates its licence texts)
recipes.notes: Lawyer-reviewed official translations of dense legalese; Creative Commons places its licence texts in the public domain and restricts only its trademarks.

recipes.title: Amazon MASSIVE intent utterances
recipes.notes: Professionally localized short assistant utterances across 51 locales. Useful filler for short-string arms.

recipes.title: WMT MQM human judgements (quality anchor)
recipes.notes: Professional MQM annotations. Never committed. Used only to calibrate our own metrics against human judgement (correlation check), not as corpus text.

recipes.title: WMT23 terminology shared task (zh-en)
recipes.notes: Do not vendor. Its experimental design is what we reuse: the same segments with the correct terminology, with proper-noun terminology, and with random terminology, which isolates whether a format's glossary channel actually changes the output.
